hypothesis: The archipelago scenario (3 lagoons, ~40px straits) was already established in incubator-trials.json as the best incubator of persistent complexity found (structure survived to min120 in 4/4 worlds; one seed held a sustained eyed golden age). This sweep varies the archipelago's GEOMETRY -- strait width (tight/loose) and lagoon count (3 vs 5) -- to find the shape that best preserves complex bodies, holding the rest of the world (founders, algae, physics) unchanged.

protocol.mechanism: Geometry varied entirely by reassigning two existing in-page function bindings (archLagoons, archTerrain) inside a browser javascript_tool exec, executed BEFORE calling initWorld('arch', SEED) for each run. No repo file was ever written to -- git diff --stat -- index.html was verified empty before the sweep and remained empty throughout (re-verified at commit e2eaaf3 after all 8 runs).
protocol.bootstrap: viewport forced to 1280x720 (R===334 verified after load); paused=true; catchupLeft=0; versusSeeds=null; heirSeeds=null; dynasty=1; parentDish=''; set before every initWorld.
protocol.environmentNote: DEVIATION FROM STANDING PROTOCOL, DISCLOSED: the browser tool serves this file (outside its project folder) as a static data: URL snapshot. navigate()/reload calls do NOT reset the page's JS realm under this tool in this environment -- verified empirically with a window marker that survived two forced reloads and a fresh-tab attempt. 'Reload every 2 runs' as literally specified was therefore not achievable. Substituted safeguard: initWorld(scn, seed) deterministically resets every gameplay-relevant global (creatures, algae, rocks via archTerrain, stepN, simT, births/deaths, lineages, chron, hist, ivLog) AND reseeds the RNG (rngS=dishSeed|0) with zero dependency on prior RNG state (rnd() is a pure mulberry32-style generator keyed only on rngS) -- so every run is fully deterministic and uncontaminated by prior runs regardless of realm reuse. A pre-existing leftover run (unrelated to this sweep, apparently residual from the original incubator-trials.json session sharing the same tab infrastructure) was discovered and discarded before any sweep run began.
protocol.chunking: 4 sequential javascript_tool execs per run (108000 steps each, ~5-25s wall time each, all under the ~30s hard ceiling), accumulating samples into window.__rt across execs; a couple of the busier E-config chunks were further split (54000 steps) as population-driven per-step cost rose. World state (stepN/simT/creatures/etc.) was never touched between chunks.
protocol.perLagoonMeasurement: The shipped lagoonOf() hardcodes a loop over the first 3 lagoons only (for(let i=0;i<3;i++)), a second hardcoded-3 quirk in the same family as the founder-seeding loop noted in the brief. Rather than overwrite that live in-engine function (which also drives the cosmetic archMigration() strait- crossing counter/flavor-text every 60 steps), per-lagoon sampling used a separate inline nearest- lagoon classifier with the same nearest-center algorithm generalized to all NLAG lagoons, so per-lagoon stats are correct for the 5-lagoon configs while the live game's own migration flavor text/counter was left exactly as shipped -- only archLagoons/archTerrain (geometry) were overridden, matching the brief's 'touches only two functions' instruction.

fieldDefinitions.withParts: creatures with sg.length>0 (>=1 body segment beyond the head)
fieldDefinitions.branched: withParts creatures where some segment o has o.par!==index-1 or o.ang!==0 (a body fork), matching the game's own 'first branch' detection logic
fieldDefinitions.paddlers: withParts creatures with a segment where o.ang!==0 and o.fin>0.5
fieldDefinitions.eyed: withParts creatures with a segment where o.eye>0.4 (checked independently of branched/paddler status -- confirmed against the archived crown run, e.g. min126: eyed 26 >> branched 7)
fieldDefinitions.mouthed: withParts creatures with a segment where o.mouth>0.4
fieldDefinitions.hidden: count of living creatures with bh>0 (at least one evolved hidden brain neuron)
fieldDefinitions.completeAnimalBar: maxParts>=2 AND eyed/pop>=25% AND paddlers>0, evaluated at a single sample, per the report brief

protocol.wipeoutRecolonizationDefinition: pop_i (per-lagoon living population) observed >0 at some sample, then ==0 at a later sample (wipedOutAtMin), then >0 again at a still-later sample (recolonizedAtMin). structureImmediatelyPresent = withParts_i>0 at the recolonization sample itself. structureWithin3SamplesAfter = withParts_i>0 at the recolonization sample or either of the next two samples (an 18-minute window). Algorithm and field names match incubator-trials.json's trial2_archipelago analysis exactly (verified: reproduces the archived '5 events, 3/5 within-3-samples' result for config A bit-for-bit from the raw samples), so B/C/D/E are directly comparable to the archived A data. For the two lagoons that start with zero founders in 5-lagoon configs (indices 3 and 4), this same state machine naturally reports their first pop_i>0 as a plain colonization, not a recolonization, since no prior wipeout precedes it.

controlReference_A.note: Config A (3 lagoons, baseline ~40px straits) was NOT rerun per instructions; this is the archived incubator-trials.json trial2_archipelago data, re-analyzed here with the identical scripts used for B/C/D/E so the league table below is apples-to-apples.

verdict: Across five geometries the original archipelago baseline (config A: three lagoons, ~40px straits) remains the best incubator of complex bodies observed in this whole line of study: it alone produced a true golden age (seed 9002, eyed >=25% of population sustained for 12 consecutive samples / 66 minutes, and the study's only repeated complete-animal touches), and none of the four new geometries in this sweep reproduced or exceeded that result even once across their combined 8 seeds. The sweep does resolve the isolation-versus-flow question cleanly: loosening the straits (config C) drives wipeout-recolonization events to zero and lifts average standing population by roughly 50% (24.6 vs 16-20 elsewhere), but that extra connectivity homogenizes the population so thoroughly that neither seed ever fixed a single eyed individual -- flow buys stability at the cost of the very drift-and-bottleneck dynamic that seems to be required to fix new structure. Tightening the straits (config B) or adding two extra refugia (D, E) both push the opposite way: they raise local wipeout frequency (B: 0.5, D: 1.4, E: 0.9 wipeouts per lagoon-seed, vs C's 0.0 and A's 0.42) while keeping the recolonists' structure-carried-back rate high to very high (B 100% immediate; D 64% immediate/86% within three samples; E 78%/78%) -- confirming the refugia mechanism itself (small isolated pockets fail locally without failing globally, then reseed each other) generalizes cleanly to both a tighter strait and a five-lagoon layout. The five-lagoon configs additionally confirm the brief's colonization hypothesis directly: in all 4 D/E seeds both initially-empty lagoons were colonized before the first sample (within 6 simulated minutes) regardless of strait tightness, and structure had already arrived with the colonists, or arrived within 18 minutes, in every one of those 8 colonization events -- fast, structure-bearing colonization is not a fragile or rare event here, it is the reliable default. Honest caveat: n=2 per new config is directional, not conclusive -- config D's headline wipeout count in particular is dominated by one dramatic near-total collapse-and-recovery in a single seed (9301), and a different pair of seeds could easily land B, D, or E's numbers in a different order. Recommendation: given that no new geometry beat the baseline on the metrics that matter most for the Paper's actual question (sustained complexity, not just any-structure survival), the baseline does appear to already sit at or very near the optimum among archipelago shapes tried so far, but config B (tight-3 straits) is the single most promising candidate for a confirmatory 4-seed run: it is the smallest perturbation from the proven baseline geometry (same 3 lagoons, only the strait narrowed), and it was the only new config to post a 100% immediate-structure-carry-back rate on every one of its wipeout events, suggesting tightening the baseline's existing straits -- rather than adding lagoons or loosening them -- is the more promising direction to push next.
